TITLE: Investigating Successor Representations as Goal Representations
PROPOSAL: We will compare the efficacy of successor representations against state observations as goal representations in a simulated environment, using a reward-free dataset of trajectories collected on a suite of benchmark robotic tasks, and evaluate their ability to facilitate efficient policy learning and robust goal-reaching performance. We will implement successor representations using a recent variant of the Neural Probabilistic Matrix Factorization (NPMPF) technique for scalable computation.
CONTROLS: We will compare these findings to those when using simple feature-based goal representations and when using the raw state observations as goal representations (a common practice in goal-conditioned RL).
COST: 100 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect successor representations to outperform state observations in facilitating efficient policy learning and robust goal-reaching performance, due to their ability to distill out relevant information and similar to prior work using them as state representations. We anticipate that successor representations will also exhibit robustness benefits for unseen goals due to their invariant nature.

PROPOSAL: We will investigate the application of information bottleneck (IB) principles for learning goal representations from reward-free data, by modifying the loss function to penalize the mutual information between the goal representation and the irrelevant parts of the observation. Specifically, we'll use a combination of normalizing flows and variational inference to compute the IB objective, and learn a goal representation capable of framing the control task in a more structured and invariant way.
CONTROLS: We'll test the effectiveness of IB against a baseline that uses a simple K-Framework for comparison, maintain the controls from the first proposal as baselines, since the baseline consists of the NPMPF and using state observations, feature-based goal specifications and excellent train default state observations
COST: 150 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We anticipate that IB-based goal representations will lead to improved policy learning and generalization, as they reduce the extraneous information in the observations and help the agent focus on the relevant aspects of the goal. This may be particularly beneficial in situations with noisy or high-dimensional observations, where IB can automatically discard redundant information.

TITLE: REVISING Goal Representation Learning in Multitask Environments
PROPOSAL NUMBER: 3
TITLE: REVISED - Multi-Modal Goal Representation Learning through Temporal Contrastive Pretraining
PROPOSAL: To explore more structured goal representations, we will use the contrastive learning framework to pretrain a goal representation model that combines features from state observations and action sequences. This multi-modal setup will enable the goal representation to learn invariant concepts to instances and learn an abstraction that is best suited to problem-solving with partial or incomplete information observed. Instead of incorporating auxiliary data, we will leverage the power of temporal contrastive learning to discover more informative and relevant goal features from the data itself. Furthermore, we will evaluate how our pre-trained goal representation performs in multitask environments, where the agent must learn to reach multiple goals simultaneously.
CONTROLS: We will compare our results to those obtained when using a simple feature-based goal representation, as well as against pre-trained representations that are specifically tailored to individual tasks.
COST: 150 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We anticipate that our pre-trained goal representation will show improved generalization and flexibility in multitask environments, and facilitate faster learning and better performance across a range of tasks.

TITLE: Examining the Role of Robustness in Goal Representations
PROPOSAL: We will investigate the impact of robust goal representations on the performance of goal-conditioned reinforcement learning agents. Specifically, we will develop a suite of noise and perturbation scenarios to test the robustness of our earlier proposed goal representations (successor representations, information bottleneck principle, and multi-modal contrastive learning) against unexpected variations in the goal or environmental conditions. We will then analyze the effects of these perturbations on policy performance, learning efficiency, and generalization.
CONTROLS: We will use the same benchmark tasks and datasets as in our previous experiments, and compare the robustness of our goal representations to a baseline representation learned using regularized regression.
COST: 120 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect that robust goal representations will exhibit superior performance and generalization in noisy and uncertain environments, such as those encountered in real-world robotics and other applications where agents may encounter unexpected perturbations.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Goal Representation Learning with Missing or Noisy Goals
PROPOSAL: We will investigate the possibility of learning goal representations from incomplete or noisy goal information. Specifically, we will introduce missing or noisy goal data into our training datasets and evaluate how our goal representations (successor representations, information bottleneck principle, multi-modal contrastive learning, and robust goal representations) perform in these challenging scenarios. We will also explore techniques for handling missing or noisy goal data, such as goal completion or imputation methods.
CONTROLS: We will use the same benchmark tasks and datasets as in our previous experiments, and compare the effectiveness of different goal completion or imputation methods in conjunction with our goal representations.
COST: 180 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We anticipate that our goal representations will be able to learn effectively from incomplete or noisy goal information, and that goal completion or imputation methods will be able to improve performance in these challenging scenarios.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Theoretical Analysis of Goal Representations
PROPOSAL: We will conduct a theoretical analysis of goal representations, focusing on the relationship between goal representations and the underlying Markov decision process (MDP). Specifically, we will explore the conditions under which different goal representations (successor representations, information bottleneck principle, etc.) are sufficient or necessary for optimal goal-reaching performance. We will also investigate the connection between goal representations and the concept of "goal alignment" in reinforcement learning.
CONTROLS: Our analysis will serve as a theoretical foundation for the experimental results presented in the paper and will help to shed light on the underlying mechanisms of goal representations in reinforcement learning.
COST: 0 GPU-hours (theoretical analysis)
PREDICTION: We expect to establish a formal connection between goal representations and optimal goal-reaching performance, and to gain a deeper understanding of the underlying principles of goal representation learning in reinforcement learning.

TITLE: Meta-Learning for Goal Representation Adaptation
PROPOSAL: We will explore the use of meta-learning to adapt goal representations to new tasks and environments. Specifically, we will use a meta-learning algorithm to learn a goal representation that can be fine-tuned to new tasks and environments, and evaluate its performance on a range of benchmark tasks and environments.
CONTROLS: We will compare our meta-learning approach to domain adaptation and domain generalization baselines.
COST: 200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect our meta-learning approach to goal representation adaptation to provide a more efficient and effective way to adapt goal representations to new tasks and environments, and to outperform traditional domain adaptation and domain generalization approaches.

PROPOSAL: Implement a successor representation learning algorithm that learns to represent the state space as a graph, where each node represents a state and the edges represent transitions between states. title: learning goal representations through proto-value gap minimization
PROPOSAL: Investigate Proto-Value Gap (PVG) Minimization as a novel approach for learning goal representations in goal-conditioned reinforcement learning (GCRL). PVG is a technique originating from the concept of proto-values, where the value difference between two states reflects the informativeness of the state transition for learning the policy. We hypothesize that if a goal representation is informative and relevant to the goal-reaching task, it should minimize the PVG between the goal and all other states in the loss landscape of the goal-conditioned policy.
CONTROLS: Against the standard goal-conditioned policy learning setup (using the original state observations as goal representations) and existing methods that explicitly learn goal representations (e.g. temporal-distance embeddings).
COST: 100 GPU-hours.
PREDICTION: Learning with PVG minimization should perform similarly or even outperform existing methods in terms of goal-reaching metric (e.g. average path length) in synthetic robot navigation and manipulation environments, while providing a theoretically grounded approach for learning goal representations. Failure could emerge if the proposed approach is too sensitive to hyperparameter tuning or model specification.

title: bottlenecked goal representations via information-theoretic autoencoders
PROPOSAL: Explore the use of Information-Theoretic Autoencoders (ITAE) to learn bottlenecked goal representations. ITAEs are a type of autoencoder that is trained to minimize the mutual information between the input and the latent space, while keeping the mutual information between the input and the reconstructed input high. By Training an ITAE on the environment observations and using the encoded representation as the goal representation, we expect to obtain a bottlenecked goal representation that discards extraneous information.
CONTROLS: Against the standard goal-conditioned policy learning setup and with the PVG minimization approach from proposal 1 (to compare against an informative yet potentially noisy goal representation).
COST: 150 GPU-hours.
PREDICTION: Using ITAE to learn goal representations should improve goal-reaching performance by discarding irrelevant information in the observations, and potentially generalize better to unseen goals. It may however struggle in environments with highly structured or partially observable state spaces, where the goal representation may become too simplistic.
